Sometimes should might be different of what you must. For example, if your program exhibits unsound behavior in safe Rust (or C++) code, it's probably a lot more practical to just change the program so that it doesn't, instead of updating the compiler, unless you happen to be a Rust compiler developer. But, at the same time, you should file an issue about it.

You can of course find C++ compiler bugs as well, although I expect that to be quite rare nowadays. But the typical case is that if a C++ program exhibits unsound behavior, there is no reasonable compiler fix for it.
